blocks.text: 1. Chunk Size Optimization

blocks.alt: The embedding model limit and content type together determine optimal chunk size

blocks.text: Chunk Size Optimization closes out the Chunking module by tying every earlier idea into a systematic approach for choosing the right chunk size.
It closes the Chunking module by tying every earlier tradeoff together into one decision process.
2. Every Topic Had A Piece Of This Answer
The tradeoff between chunk size and context, raised back in Why Chunking, ran through every strategy in this module, each touching chunk size from a different angle.
This topic gathers those scattered pieces into one systematic decision process.
3. Starting From The Embedding Model's Limit

blocks.alt: An embedding model has a max token limit

blocks.text: As with the whole documents are too big problem in Why Chunking, the embedding model's input limit sets an absolute ceiling on chunk size.
No chunk size decision can ignore that hard ceiling.
4. Matching Size To Content Type

blocks.alt: A short FAQ and a long article need different chunk sizes

blocks.text: Within that ceiling, dense technical text needs smaller chunks than narrative, flowing prose.
As with when fixed chunking is enough in Fixed Chunking, content structure shapes the right size.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Content type","Typical chunk size tendency"],"rows":[["Dense technical text","Smaller chunks, one concept at a time"],["Narrative, flowing prose","Larger chunks, preserving flow and context"]]}

blocks.text: 5. Small Chunks Versus Large Chunks Revisited

blocks.alt: Small precise chunks are compared against large chunks with more context

blocks.text: As with the retrieval precision tradeoff in Why Chunking, smaller chunks retrieve with sharper precision.
Larger chunks, by contrast, preserve more surrounding context per retrieved result.

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: Every strategy in this module, from fixed chunking through contextual chunking, offered its own answer to this same underlying question. Chunk size optimization is the practice of choosing deliberately rather than by accident.

blocks.text: 6. Empirical Tuning Over Guessing

blocks.alt: A guessed size is compared against a size measured through evaluation

blocks.text: As with measuring overlap effectiveness in Chunk Overlap, testing several chunk sizes against real queries beats guessing a single number.
Measurable retrieval quality, the subject of a later module on evaluation, should drive the final choice.

blocks.title: warn
blocks.content: Picking a chunk size once during initial development and never revisiting it risks locking in a suboptimal choice permanently, since the right size depends on the actual content and query patterns a system ends up handling.

blocks.text: 7. Chunk Size Interacts With Retrieval Count

blocks.alt: Chunk size and retrieval count k together determine total context used

blocks.text: Smaller chunks mean a retrieval system typically needs to fetch more of them to cover the same amount of content.
As with retrieval using embeddings in What Is RAG, chunk size and retrieval count move together, not independently.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Chunk size choice","Effect on retrieval count needed"],"rows":[["Smaller chunks","More chunks typically need to be retrieved to cover a topic"],["Larger chunks","Fewer chunks typically needed, each carrying more content"]]}

blocks.text: 8. Building A Practical Checklist
Combining the embedding limit, content type, the precision versus context tradeoff, and empirical testing forms a repeatable process.
That turns what looked like a single arbitrary number into a defensible engineering decision.
9. Recognizing How To Approach Chunk Size For A New Pipeline

blocks.alt: Starting a new RAG pipeline points toward tuning chunk size empirically

blocks.text: Starting with a reasonable default and testing against real queries works for most pipelines.
Highly specialized or unusual content may need a custom size chosen through dedicated experimentation.
10. Worked Example
The example below demonstrates comparing retrieval results across two candidate chunk sizes.

code.content:
document = (
    "Machine learning models require large amounts of labeled training data. "
    "Data quality matters as much as data quantity for model performance. "
    "Once trained, models are evaluated on a held out test set. "
    "Evaluation metrics guide decisions about further model improvements."
)

def fixed_chunk(text, chunk_size):
    return [text[i:i + chunk_size] for i in range(0, len(text), chunk_size)]

def fake_relevance_score(chunk, query_terms):
    # relevance density: fraction of chunk words matching the query
    words = set(chunk.lower().split())
    overlap = len(words & query_terms)
    density = overlap / max(len(words), 1)
    return density

query_terms = {"evaluation", "metrics", "model"}

for size in [40, 100]:
    chunks = fixed_chunk(document, size)
    scores = [fake_relevance_score(c, query_terms) for c in chunks]
    best_score = max(scores)
    print(f"Chunk size {size}: {len(chunks)} chunks, best relevance density={best_score:.2f}")

print("\nComparing scores across sizes reveals which chunk size actually produces the sharpest, most relevant match for this query.")

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: Running this example shows different chunk sizes producing different relevance density scores for the same query, rather than assuming any single size is universally correct.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Choosing a chunk size once early on and never testing whether it actually performs well.
Ignoring the embedding model's hard input limit when selecting a chunk size.
Using the same chunk size for both dense technical content and flowing narrative text.
Forgetting that chunk size and retrieval count are linked, not independent settings.

blocks.text: 12. Chunking: Module Complete

items: Why Chunking introduced why documents need to be split before embedding at all.
Fixed Chunking covered the simplest strategy, splitting by a fixed character or token count.
Recursive Chunking covered falling back through an ordered list of separators for smarter cuts.
Semantic Chunking covered splitting at points where the actual topic shifts.
Sliding Window Chunking covered preserving context through overlapping windows.
Sentence Chunking covered splitting strictly along sentence boundaries.
Parent-Child Chunking covered searching small child chunks while retrieving their larger parent.
Hierarchical Chunking covered following a document's own multi level structure.
Contextual Chunking covered enriching chunk text with summaries and heading context.
Chunk Overlap covered treating shared text between chunks as its own tunable decision.
Chunk Size Optimization closed the module by tying every tradeoff into one systematic process.
